51:38: Similarly (for those who ponder and reflect) there are signs in the story of Moses, when We sent him to Pharaoh with clear laws and rationale.
51:39: But the Pharaoh, feeling proud of his power, turned away from these Laws and said about Moses, “He is either very clever and a liar; or he has gone mad.\"
51:40: So in reprisal of their crimes, Our Law of Mukafat seized him and his forces; and their fleet drowned at their own hands. They deserved this.
51:41: Like this (as signs of Our Law of Mukafat) in the story of people of Aad We sent against them the chastisement of blasting winds.
51:42: Such was the intensity of that punishment that whatever it touched was reduced to dust and ashes. Nothing was left intact.
51:43: And in the story of the tribe of Thamud (there are signs of Our Law of Mukafat), We gave them respite and told them to enjoy the sustenance provided to them during this period.
51:44: But they did not take advantage of this respite and insolently defied the Divine Laws.
51:45: Hence (when the time for judgment came) a devastating earthquake overtook them. (All their haughty claims perished and) They were neither left with enough strength to stand up after falling once, nor to call any one for help. Who can render help against the Divine Law of Mukafat?
51:46: And before them was the nation of Noah, who too had adopted an erroneous way of life (as a result of which they were destroyed).
51:47: (This is Our Law of Mukafat, under which earlier communities came to such an end. Everything in this universe is busy making the Divine Law effective. That is why) With Our power and strength We have built the universe that is spread out in the cosmos. The expanse of Our power has no boundaries.
51:48: And earth was spacious and spread out wide so that it would be comfortable for Our creations. See how beautiful and fine the comforts We create are!
51:49: We have created everything with its counterpart, so that each pairs with the other; and you may ponder.
51:50: We have explained you all this so that you become aware of the universality of Allah’s authority and hasten to adopt the path indicated by Him, leaving aside all other erroneous ways. My duty (the Rasool\'s) is to continue warning you about the disastrous consequences of your erroneous way of life.
51:51: You should not set up any other authority as partners with Allah. No one else wields any authority or power besides Him; and I have been commanded by Him to give you clear warning about the outcome of your erroneous ways!
51:52: (In reply they say various ridiculous things about you. However since you are not the first Rasool, the attitude of these opponents is also not unusual.) In the past also, the people to whom Rusul were sent told them that they (the Rusul) were either liars, deceitful or insane.
51:53: From such events it seems as if every passing generation will be the next one to adopt a behaviour which leads to a revolutionary attitude. The fact remains that their selfish ends instigate these people to rebel against the Divine Laws (and since the mentality is always the same, the reaction to this revolutionary call is also manifested in similar manner).
51:54: Therefore you should not be grieved by their bevahiour. Continue fulfilling of your own programme, irrespective of them. You will not be blamed for this (because you have done your duty of conveying the Divine Message to them).
51:55: And always keep on reminding Jamaat-ul-Momineen about the Divine Laws. Such reminders will be a source of strength for them; and this method will prove beneficial to them.
51:56: Remember the fact that the very objective of the creation of human beings, whether civilized urbanites or uncivilized nomads of the desert, would be fulfilled if they develop their potential abilities by following the Divine Laws (and then devote themselves to establishing the universal social order for nurturing all mankind).
51:57: The establishment of this Order will not benefit Allah the Almighty. It will bring good only to you. He does not want anything from His subjects; neither food nor any other sustenance.
51:58: What can He expect from His subjects? He is the One Who Himself provides sustenance to all creation. All power and strength belongs to Him. (Similarly the social order that is established according to His Laws will also not ask for anything for its own benefit. It will only work for benefit of mankind.)
51:59: But if these people (do not fulfill the objective of their creation and) rebel against it, then their end result will be the same as that of earlier nations which had adopted a similar attitude.However, this will appear in its own time. These people should not be in haste, for the moment the cumulative effects are accounted they will be doomed.
51:60: Thus an awful doom awaits the people who deny the Hour of Judgment and those who have no faith in the Divine Law of Mukafat.

If they have any similar claim, let them prove it.)\n\n*1- It is the peculiarity of wahi that no human being can get it by himself.  It is always revealed by God to man.  However the saints/sufis (the mystics) claim that they can get direct divine knowledge through their own work and effort.  (This is what is called kashf and ilham or divine inspiration).  This claim is completely against Quranic injunctions.  No human can obtain divine knowledge.  That knowledge was revealed by God to whosoever He wished.  This process has been permanently discontinued after Rasool Allah (Muhammad PBUH).
52:39: (On the one hand they claim to have access to the heavens. But on the other look at the level of their intellect, particularly when) They also say that Allah has offspring, and that too daughters. However for their own selves they (prefer to) have sons.
52:40: Or is it that they do not agree with you, because you demand some reward or wages (for what you preach); and because they are worried that they would be burdened with this penalty, they want to remain away from you (68:40).
52:41: Or do they not want to profess Eiman because they have acquired knowledge of future happenings through which they know that whatever you say is unlikely to happen?
52:42: (None of the above is the reason of their attitude. In actual fact they oppose your mission because it affects their selfish interests and they do not have the courage to say so openly. At the same time) They are conspiring a plot to trap you. However, let them do so; for they themselves will fall in those traps (and no harm will come to you).
52:43: They think that their false gods (deities and saints) will help them. This is simply their whim. No one other than Allah wields any authority in the universe and He is above and beyond being ascribed any associates.
52:44: (They are so deeply involved in their whims and wishful thinking that while doom and destruction has surmounted them from all sides, they believe that their gods:deities will turn their miseries into comforts. They would consider it to be a massive cloud of rain that is coming to irrigate their fields.
52:45: (There seems no scope for them to come to the right path. Anyhow you have done your duty of conveying the message to them. Now) Leave them alone until they are struck with lightening and doom befalls them.
52:46: At that time, neither will their planning be of any avail to them nor will anyone be able to help them.
52:47: This chastisement will take place in this world. However there is another one waiting for them in the world hereafter, but most are not aware of it.
52:48: (So leave them to their plight and) Continue striving hard for the establishment and strengthening of the Divine Order, with complete composure and steadfastness. You are always within Our sight and We keep a watch over you.
52:49: Remain ever busy, from morning till evening and through the night till the stars begin to wane, making this Nizam-e-Rabubiat worthy of all praise and Hamd (50:41).

Do they not always provide you the same guidance? Have they ever left you confused? So whatever opinion you have with regard to the stars, it should be exactly the same in respect of Wahi. 53:3: Whatever he tells you in his capacity as a Rasool, he does not say it on his own. He only narrates the Wahi revealed to him from the Almighty. 53:6: Not only does the Almighty possess unlimited powers, but He is also aware of the various ups and downs of life. 53:7: (Due to Wahi) He also reached the pinnacle of knowledge, beyond human intellect or wisdom (81:23);
53:8: He thus came very close to the absolute realities of the universe and deeply understood the Divine Laws, becoming in unison with them.
53:9: As a result of this closeness and unison, he became Almighty\'s companion in the human world, to fulfil His Programme (8:17). This closeness was similar to the strengthening of the bond of friendship, just like drawing two bows together, both appearing almost one and then together shooting the arrow. This example shows the close affinity between the Rasool and Allah the Almighty. In fact however, it was far stronger and deeper.
53:10: In this way He revealed to His votary all that He wanted to reveal (for the guidance of mankind).
53:11: The knowledge given to the Rasool through Wahi is unlike that which the eyes perceive; and the heart too cannot decide whether it is reality or a delusion. In Nabi’s case, his conscience confirms whatever his eyes see. (That is why Nabi is the first one to profess Eiman on the truthfulness of his Wahi ~ 2:285; 6:164.)
53:12: Now say, how can you challenge him about the realities of Wahi when he has actually seen whatever he talks about; and when you cannot even comprehend his status!
53:13: (Furthermore the state of Wahi is not that of a dream which cannot be experienced for the second time, in the same sequence and detail.) However, the Nabi’s eyes can see again the phenomena he has seen once. (Therefore for him the seeing of realities is not the same as dreaming. Wahi is not a dream. It is the observance of real facts.)
53:14: The source of Wahi is Divine knowledge; and this is the point which completely bewilders human intellect and wisdom. (Wahi is not the developed stage of human intellect. It is not a creation of human intellect. Its source is beyond human reach and that is why intellect cannot explain it.)
53:15: (However, the fact that human intellect cannot comprehend the nature of Nabuwwah, does not mean that any benefit cannot be drawn from it.) However if one spends life according to the guidance of Wahi, it will take him straight to Jannah.)
53:16: (Unlike other human beings) The state of Nabi is such that even when he is in that valley of \'bewilderment\' surrounded by Divine Knowledge, his eyes do not falter or stray. Whereas Divine Knowledge is unlimited, as desired by God the knowledge bestowed on the Nabi through Wahi is limited. Hence it could be considered as a part of Divine Knowledge, but not the whole of it. Although the knowledge granted by Wahi is far ahead of that of humans, it still is limited in terms of Divine Knowledge. Nabi’s perception cannot cross that limit.)

(He saw with his own eyes the wonderful and sublime revolution that was about to come in the human world; that was bound to topple the mighty superpowers and authorities of kings, priests and capitalists; and that which ultimately freed man from the bonds of the Pharaohs, Kora and Hamans ~ 17:1; 20:23-24; 7:156.)
53:19: (Tell them that on the one hand is this Divine message which has been revealed from the Almighty, whose knowledge and wisdom are limitless, and which is being presented to you by this Rasool who himself is the embodiment of all human virtues; and on the other is your way of life wherein you bow before statues carved by yourselves out of stone!) 53:21: (And have you ever pondered over your belief that these deities are the daughters of Almighty? The very belief that God has children is utterly ridiculous. Furthermore, you state that) The Almighty has daughters, whereas you have the sons!
53:22: Just imagine how preposterous this apportioning is, particularly as it is based on sheer ignorance.
53:23: Remember that the factual position of these deities is that they are only names which you and your forefathers have devised (7:71). Allah the Almighty has not bestowed any warrant for them (nor can any proof or evidence for such beliefs be given rationally). These people just follow their assumptions simply to satisfy their wishful thinking. (O Rasool) whatever you present (on the other hand) is a code of guidance which your Rabb bestowed on you (and it is totally based on knowledge and facts).
53:24: Each one of you goes to these deities to fulfill your wishes; and you are under the impression that they would be fulfilled.  Just think)  Is it possible that every person’s wishes can be fulfilled?  (For example, how can the conflicting desires of two persons be fulfilled?  This is what always happens in a system in which every individual works for his own interest.  Individual interests do conflict.  However the Divine Order keeps in view the collective good of all human beings and therefore there is no clash of individual interests.  Another result of this collective system is that) Everyone gets immediate benefits, and one’s future life will also be bright and successful.
53:25: Each one of you goes to these deities to fulfill your wishes; and you are under the impression that they would be fulfilled. 53:26: These people have also made as their deities the various forces of nature in the universe such as air, water, fire, clouds, lightning or thunder.   Tell them that making these forces deities will not bring them any success.  Even if they imagine that such deities are with them, they will not obtain any benefit.  The only way they can be of any use to them is if these forces are utilized according to the Law of Nature; and in unison with the overall programme of the Divine Will.
53:27: (The above attitude is based on knowledge and reality.  However) These people consider these heavenly forces to be their gods:deities and give them feminine names.  Only the people who have no faith in the Law of Mukafat and in life hereafter would do such things.  (The one who believes in the law of cause and effect would never get involved in such superstitions.)
53:28: Their attitude is not based on knowledge and reality but on mere guesswork.  It is obvious that such guesswork cannot be compared to reality and truth (6:149).  Such guesswork may work in the era of ignorance, but it loses impact when faced with  knowledge and truth.
53:29: So the people who have no ideal higher than worldly comfort and gains, turn away and leave Our Code of Life, (O Rasool!) You should stay away from them. (However remain actively involved in the fulfillment of your programme.)
53:30: How can the people whose extent of knowledge is so low (that they consider statues carved out of stone with their own hands to be their gods and prostrate before the heavenly forces) accept the truthfulness of a Deen which is based totally on knowledge and facts and which gives human beings the highest status in the universe? (But you should not be disheartened by their attitude.) Your Rabb knows fully well who goes on the straight path; and who strays leaving the guidance aside.
53:31: (The results would be compiled according to the course a person takes.) This is because everything in the heavens and on earth is continuously compiling the consequences of one’s deeds; producing negative results for those creating chaos and disorder; and producing positive and pleasant results for those who lead a righteous life (11:7; 45:22).
53:32: These people (who lead righteous lives) avoid the serious offenses that slow down the growth of human personality and the actions which spread abominations. However in a situation when one realises this and immediately corrects oneself (7:201), or even if he makes an unintentional mistake (and thereafter corrects himself), then one is forgiven the consequences of such actions. (In other words this means that) The weight of their good deeds is so heavy that it provides protection against the ill-effects of minor unintentional mistakes. This shows the abounding magnanimity of the Divine Law of Mukafat (4:31; 42:37). This is the Law of the Almighty Who is fully aware of human weaknesses as well as their potential abilities. He knows the stages that life has gone through from being inanimate matter to becoming human beings; and how many formations the fetus attained in the mother\'s womb. He knows what hampers the development of human ‘self’ and what helps it grow. This is the very criterion for adjudging the depth of the divine injunctions in one\'s personality. The judgement should not be according to one\'s own devised standards. (The one and the only touchstone is Allah’s Book and not any man-made standards ~ 91:7-10; 93:17-18.)
53:33: (In order to judge the extent of development of one\'s personality the basic standard is how much one gives away for meeting the needs of other people. Despite such an attitude they judge their own deeds by their self­-devised measures and consider themselves to be very noble and pious.

53:35: Do these people have knowledge of the unseen that has told them that the standard adopted by them is the correct one?
53:36: Do they not know that the standard laid down in the Quran by Us is the same one that was conveyed to mankind through various Anbia; and the same that was contained in the Book revealed to Moses;
53:37: And the one revealed earlier to Abraham who in his person was the embodiment of obedience; and who proved true to every commitment he made?
53:38: The principles and standards that were revealed to previous Anbia and which are now being repeated in the Quran were:\n(i) No one shall carry the burden of another person. Everyone is responsible for his own actions and the development of one\'s ‘self’ can take place only through one’s own deeds;
53:39: (ii) A man (is entitled) to receive only that for which he has strived. (The results will be proportionate to the effort. According to the Divine Standard, the compensation should only be for labour.)
53:40: (iii) Nobody’s toils will go waste. They will certainly see the results.
53:41: (iv) There will be no shortfall in the reward of one\'s labour. Everyone will get full reward for one’s efforts.
53:42: (v) The ultimate objective and goal of human life is to establish Nizam-e-Rabubiyyat for the collective good. The semblance of divine attributes is reflected in every individual (as far as is humanly possible) and every human affair is decided according to the Divine Laws (79:44).
53:43: These are the fundamental principles according to which a nation lives a life full of comforts and pleasures; while others live in depression, lamenting in a house of mourning.
53:44: The life and death of nations is regulated by these firm unchangeable laws. The nation which follows these laws survives while the one that violates them perishes.
53:45: (The life and death of nations is subject to these Divine Laws in a manner similar to an individual’s birth, growth and death.) According to the same law, the birth of a human being takes place when the reproductive materials intermix following which the males and females are born.
53:46: (The life and death of nations is subject to these Divine Laws in a manner similar to an individual’s birth, growth and death.) According to the same law, the birth of a human being takes place when the reproductive materials intermix following which the males and females are born.
53:47: Up to this level of creation human beings and animals are alike. However later, He raises a human being in a totally different way. (He instills in him a ray of divine energy that enables him to exercise choice and discretion.)
53:48: Subsequently the Almighty\'s Nizam-e-Rabubiyyat makes arrangements to fulfill the basic necessities of life in a manner that no one remains dependent on others. He bestows on him things which give peace and tranquillity.
53:49: Up to this stage, as far as means of nourishment are concerned, man and animal are alike. But He has also granted intellect and conscience to the human beings. 53:51: And also the tribe of Thamud. None of them survived.
53:52: Even before them the people of Noah were destroyed. All these tribes perished because they rebelled against the Divine Laws and perpetuated \"zulm\" on weaker people.
53:53: All the tribes which adopted such an attitude were completely destroyed; and their habitations were depopulated and became ruins.
53:54: Their destruction was the outcome of their deeds; and it came from all sides encircling them completely.
53:55: In light of this historical evidence, ask these people about how many different powers of the Divine Law they dispute or question?
53:56: These are the consequences of your deeds about which this Rasool cautions you; just like how the Rusul of earlier nations warned their people. (They ignored their warnings and perished; if these people also ignore warnings they too will be annihilated.)
53:57: The hour of destruction which was fast approaching has become imminent.
53:58: No power in this world can stall it; but if even now they follow and obey the Divine Law it could be averted.
53:59: Ask them, “Do you still marvel at the things that are being told to you? Are you not convinced that they are bound to happen?
53:60: “And keep laughing. Actually if you knew the reality you would weep; but no one applies his mind seriously.
53:61: “It is for this reason that you are rebellious and not changing your attitude. You take life only as fun and indulge in pleasures.
53:62: Do not do this. The time is not out yet; you still have time to bow before the Divine Laws and obey them (and you will be saved from the coming doom).”
54:1: The Hour of Revolution (about which they have been warned for a long time) is just around. The power and might of these opposing Arabs will come to an end and their flag (carrying the insignia of the moon) will be torn to pieces.
54:2: Many of the signs of the coming revolution have appeared before them, but because of their rebellious attitude they do not seriously ponder over them. Instead they turn away saying, “These are the same old fables that we had been hearing for a longtime.” (46:11)
54:3: They contradict and belie everything concerning this Revolution and continue to follow their own selfish interests. 54:10: Whereupon he called to his Rabb and prayed \"These people have overtaken me. So take revenge (for their unjust oppression).”
54:11: So We opened up the floodgates of heavy rains from the skies.
54:12: And the earth burst open with springs. The water from the earth and the sky collected together (and rose) to take the form of a flood, for a purpose destined according to Our Law of Mukafat.
54:13: And We made Noah (and his companions) board a vessel made of broad planks and nails (and tied with ropes).
54:14: And in this mighty flood it sailed under Our supervision (so they remained safe while their opponents drowned). This was the outcome of their refusal to accept Noah\'s suggestion (when he was warning them about the impending flood which they took as a joke. While he was making a boat people were laughing at it. People who do not take safety measures despite knowing and seeing the on-coming catastrophe are bound to get destroyed.)
54:15: We have preserved this episode for those who want to learn a lesson. Is there anyone who will reflect on how the warnings given by Us come true; and how Our chastisement faces them as stark reality?
54:16: We have preserved this episode for those who want to learn a lesson. Is there anyone who will reflect on how the warnings given by Us come true; and how Our chastisement faces them as stark reality?
54:17: For those who want to take advice, We have made this Quran easy to understand. Is their anyone who will reflect on it and take advice?
54:18: Likewise the people of Aad belied Our Law of Mukafat, but soon realized how Our warnings come true and how suffering is inflicted.
54:19: We let loose on them the suffering of a raging stormy wind. That was the Day of a violent disaster; one that destroyed them forever (41:16).
54:20: The storm swept the people off their feet and threw them far away, as if they were trunks of uprooted palm trees being thrown here and there (69:7).
54:21: Therefore consider the truth of Our warning and the severity of Our chastisement!
54:22: (After keeping this historical evidence in mind, consider how) We have indeed made this Quran simple and easy to understand. Thus is there anyone who wants to reflect on and take lessons from it?
54:23: Similarly, the people of Thamud belied Our warnings,
54:24: And said, \"Should we follow a man who is alone (without any group behind him)? (If we did so and left our clan to follow him, this would be tantamount to unnecessarily calling for doom and destruction.) The only person who would commit such an error is one who, finding no way of safety, falls into a ditch like a blind or mad man unable to realize what is right or wrong for him!
54:25: \"Think of how the Almighty, leaving aside so many mighty personalities, has selected him (Saleh) as the one to receive His Wahi. To us he seems to be a small conceited person (who calls himself Allah’s Rasool just to gain importance).\"
54:26: (We told Saleh not to be disheartened by their severe taunts.) They will very soon know who in fact is a liar or conceited person!
54:27: You should wait for some time and remain firm and steadfast. Their promise that they would allow the she camel to graze and drink when she returns will be a test of their commitment (whether it is true or otherwise). When they break their promise it will become the cause of their destruction.
54:28: You should explicitly tell them that according to the agreement, all cattle can drink in their turn; and likewise this she-camel will in its turn come to the drinking place.
54:29: They told the whole story to their companion (the chieftain). (He lost his temper and said, \"How can his she-camel be treated like our own animals?” With great arrogance) He stretched his hand and cruelly killed her.
54:30: (This was the final sign showing that their rebellious attitude had crossed all limits. Thereafter came the time for their destruction and they saw with their own eyes) How true Our warning is; and how severe Our chastisement!
54:31: We sent chastisement in the form of a severe earthquake (7:78). They were completely crushed and reduced to crumbling twigs, like those of a decayed fence destroyed by the force of a severe wind.(The fence safeguards crops; but when it becomes too weak to withstand the wind how can it protect others? Nations that adopt a rebellious course of life appear strong from the outside. However they are all hollow and unstable on the inside and thus cannot withstand the jolt of even one unfavourable circumstance.)
54:32: By narrating this historical evidence We have made the Quran simple and easy to understand. Therefore is there anyone who, after pondering over this, will not take advantage of it and direct his life on to the right course?
54:33: Likewise, the people of Lot belied Our messengers who cautioned them about their erroneous way of life.
54:34: We sent on them a violent storm of volcanic stones that left no one alive, except Lot and his companions whom We had rescued from there early in the morning (51:32-34).
54:35: This was a favour from Us (to Lot and his companions). But the favour was not granted easily to them. It was the outcome of them accepting the truth and acknowledging Our guidance with gratitude. Whoever takes this course of action receives a similar reward and remains safe from calamities.
54:36: Lot had warned his people time and again to remain conscious of the Divine Law of Mukafat, but they ignored as an empty threat. On the contrary they started arguing with him.
54:37: When Lot’s guests came to visit him, they (the people of Lot) approached the visitors with evil designs. They were in fact becoming crazed by their lustful feelings (and were not ready to listen to anything that Lot was saying. Hence We told them) Now get ready to taste the results of your misdeeds and see for yourselves the doom which you were cautioned about and which you thought was a mere lie. How true it comes!
54:38: Therefore, early in the morning an abiding calamity overtook them.
54:39: (And they were told) \"Now you can taste my punishment and see for yourselves how my warnings come true.\"
54:40: By narrating these episodes in the Quran, We have made it easy to understand. Is there anyone who is not willing to ponder over it and take some lessons?
54:41: Likewise We also sent Our messengers to the Pharaoh’s nation. The messengers cautioned them about the disastrous effects of their misdeeds.
54:42: They rejected each one of Our Commandments, whereupon the mighty grip of Our Law of Mukafat seized them with full strength and force.
54:43: (O Rasool! After narrating these stories of previous generations,) Ask your opponents and those who deny the truth, \"Are you in anyway better or more powerful in strength and authority than the nations mentioned afore (as a result of which they were destroyed, while you will remain safe)? Or has any immunity been granted to you in Our scriptures?\"
54:44: They are under the impression that all the tribes will be united and help each other in opposing you (and that in this way no one can harm them).
